newsitem.title: UK: IPE Brent rises on Iraq fears, OPEC in background.
newsitem.headline: IPE Brent rises on Iraq fears, OPEC in background.

text.p: IPE Brent crude oil futures opened firmer on Monday as OPEC ministers arrived in Vienna for this week's OPEC conference and dealers in London said new tensions between Iraq and the UN were pushing prices higher.
August Brent crude oil stood 19 cents a barrel firmer at 0950 GMT and was trading at $17.86, while July gas oil was $1.75 a tonne up at $160.25.
"There is some concern about the U.N. threat and maybe a bit of concern about the OPEC meeting which is prompting some nervous short covering," one broker said.
"OPEC is making people a bit cautious but it is not really a big factor in this morning's higher price."
The U.N. Security Council adopted a resolution over the weekend threatening Iraq with further sanctions if it does not allow U.N. arms inspectors to search sensitive sites.
It also suspended until the end of October regular 60 day reviews of current sanctions.
But traders noted that the threatened sanctions were not aimed directly at the recently renewed $2 billion oil-for-food deal between the U.N. and Iraq.
"This is not in itself going to affect the deal and I think there is a bit of hype in the market at the moment," a broker said.
But Baghdad has also said it will not resume exports under the renewed deal until $800 million of revenue from sales under the last deal are released to buy humanitarian provisions.
Technical traders said they expected Brent would test higher today but would find a large obstacle to any upwards movement at around the $18.00 level.

This corresponds to two gaps formed on the continuation chart last week between $17.98 and $18.00. These lie at the base of what is known as a bear island reversal on the chart, which has recently been casting a gloomy shadow on the market.
